qs.q: A patient with disseminated histoplasmosis shows macrophages filled with small yeast forms. Which specific structural feature of the fungus facilitates survival within these reticuloendothelial cells?
o: Produces melanin to resist oxidative stress
Buds rapidly to increase intracellular population
Forms large chlamydospores for host protection
Secretes specific proteases to digest phagosomes
Inhibits fusion of phagolysosome in macrophages
qs.e: Histoplasma capsulatum survives in macrophages by inhibiting phagolysosome fusion, allowing it to persist in the cytoplasm.

qs.q: A 34-year-old man with AIDS presents with disseminated histoplasmosis. Intracellular yeast forms are identified within phagolysosomes of macrophages. Which virulence property of this organism is primarily responsible for its intracellular survival?
qs.e: Resistance to phagocytic killing allows the pathogen to persist and multiply within the hostile environment of macrophages. Inhibition of phagolysosome fusion is utilized by other intracellular pathogens like Mycobacteria rather than dimorphic fungi.
qs.s: Mycoses: Fungal Pathogenesis, Virulence & Host Immune Defense: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following represents a recognized primary treatment regimen for chronic or systemic histoplasmosis?
o: Dapsone combined with daily streptomycin injections
Flucytosine 100 mg per kilogram daily for 2 weeks
Oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for 6 to 12 weeks
Fluconazole 400 mg daily for 8 to 10 weeks duration
qs.e: Oral itraconazole at 200 mg/day for 6 to 12 weeks is a standard treatment for histoplasmosis. Fluconazole and flucytosine are primary treatments associated with cryptococcosis.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of histoplasmosis?
qs.e: Histoplasmosis is not transmitted from person to person. It is acquired by inhaling spores from the mycelial phase found in soil, particularly associated with bird and bat droppings.

qs.q: NOT a characteristic of histoplasmosis: Histoplasmosis is acquired from environmental exposure (soil/bird-bat droppings), not person-to-person. ---
qs.e: Histoplasmosis is acquired from environmental sources and does not transmit person-to-person.
